headline: The GPU is faster per iteration from about \(2.0\) million cells: on the largest mesh (4,752,000 cells) one iteration takes \(3.80\,\mathrm{s}\) on the best CPU setup (GAMG DIC-GS, 8 ranks) and \(3.37\,\mathrm{s}\) with the pressure solved on the GPU (8 ranks), a factor \(1.13\); the pressure solve alone takes \(1.44\) against \(0.87\,\mathrm{s}\) (factor \(1.65\)). Both give the same converged forces.
notes: GPU study. The GPU is faster per iteration from about \(2.0\) million cells: on the largest mesh (4,752,000 cells) one iteration takes \(3.80\,\mathrm{s}\) on the best CPU setup (GAMG DIC-GS, 8 ranks) and \(3.37\,\mathrm{s}\) with the pressure solved on the GPU (8 ranks), a factor \(1.13\); the pressure solve alone takes \(1.44\) against \(0.87\,\mathrm{s}\) (factor \(1.65\)). Both give the same converged forces. See the GPU study report.
Pressure share. On the CPU the pressure solve takes G16 \(35\,\%\), L3 \(26\,\%\), G36 \(30\,\%\), L4 \(32\,\%\), G60 \(38\,\%\) of an iteration; that bounds what any pressure-solver change can gain.
